summary: P1.4b AlembicAgent in-process flatten — re-point the AlembicAgent in-process submit path to the canonical validateAgainst with the now-shipped profile axis, closing the CG-4 in-process parity gap. This is a SCOPED behavior change (a tightening), so follow the section C.4 discipline strictly. Today AlembicAgent src/tools/runtime/handlers/knowledge.ts handleSubmit runs the looser validateSubmitParams (length and presence only, around line 283, called near line 101) then gateway.create (around line 175) which only runs Core stage-3; stages 1 and 2 never run in-process. STEP 1 PRODUCER-PROMPT-FIRST (mandatory, do this before enabling the gate): upgrade the in-process producer prompt in src/agent/prompts/insightProducer.ts (around lines 133-142, buildProducerStyleGuide plus PRODUCER_SUBMIT_FIELD_CONTRACT) to render from renderGuidance('in-process', undefined, profile) so the producer KNOWS the new rules (the verb allowlist, the contrast markers, markdown floor plus code-or-file-ref, the cheap grounding) before any gate enforces them — this prevents the in-process agent from reverse-engineering the gate. STEP 2 enable the gate: before gateway.create, call validateAgainst([item], {stage:'all', path:'in-process', profile: resolveAuthoringProfile(context), sourceRefResolver: the in-process fs resolver, dimensionId: dimMeta id}) and on violations return the existing in-process reject envelope shape; the profile is resolved by resolveAuthoringProfile from context, so in-process AI dev without a cold-start session runs the OPPORTUNISTIC profile (all content gates plus cheap grounding, but NOT the 3-distinct-files floor and NOT session-scope) — the lighter bar that resolves the C.4 over-tightening concern. Wire the in-process fs sourceRefResolver so the kept grounding (SOURCE_REF_LINE_MISSING format, fs resolution SOURCE_REF_NOT_FOUND and LINE_OUT_OF_RANGE, SNIPPET_MISMATCH) actually runs; verify dimMeta id and any session plumbing exist (for opportunistic, session-scope is off, but the fs resolver is needed). Fold the validateSubmitParams length checks into the spec content gate and remove the now-redundant thin pre-check (or keep it only as a cheap fast-fail that the authoritative validateAgainst supersedes). STEP 3 regression (C.4): capture a corpus of in-process recipes that PASS today under the length-only bar, run them through the new opportunistic validateAgainst, and DOCUMENT exactly which now fail (expected: only content problems — missing verb, missing contrast markers, markdown too thin — far smaller than a cold-start tightening); this is the proof the tightening is bounded. STEP 4 parity test (section 12.5, new standing tripwire): for a fixture candidate corpus under the SAME profile, host-agent validateAgainst and in-process validateAgainst must return byte-identical verdicts (violations arrays equal). Acceptance on node 22: AlembicAgent build:check green; the producer-prompt-renders-from-module test; the in-process gate re-point test; the currently-passing-corpus regression with the documented new-reject set; the host-vs-in-process parity test; full AlembicAgent test green. Discipline: cold-start profile stays byte-identical (the host path is unaffected); opportunistic is the DECLARED lighter bar not a relaxation; gates not relaxed beyond the declared profile; main only, no push or tag or version bump. Producer-consumer: you consume the shipped Core profile model (8771524) via @alembic/core/knowledge; the main-body Alembic GatewayActionRegistry re-point (P1.4c) is the second in-process entry and follows as a separate wave. Reconcile with the P1-Plugin decision that session-scope stays a host-side precondition: in-process opportunistic has session-scope OFF so there is no conflict. Backfill the AlembicAgent commit, the producer-prompt proof, the in-process re-point diff, the currently-passing-corpus regression result (the new-reject set), the parity test result, and raw build and test output. If the tightening would reject a recipe you believe should pass, STOP and return needs-review with the case so the controller can rule.
